Aldous Vane is a billionaire senior executive at Omnicore, and the main antagonist in Beacon's Circadia Valley.

## Background

Aldous Vane was the Chief Innovation Officer of Omnicore, a huge tech company in Circadia Valley that seemingly has its hands in everything but specifically does “targeted search and cross-platform verticals.” He has a long-standing rivalry with Magnus Quill, which only fuels his desire to acquire Tobin’s algorithm. For Aldous, bigger is better – and money is no object.

Cinder Row Shuffle is the first episode in Season 2 of the Beacon series Circadia Valley, and the ninth episode overall. It originally aired on April 12, 2015.

## Plot

The Fernwright guys are wined and dined by every venture capitalist under the sun, while Nia adjusts to a new managing partner at Meridian Capital as the company faces major changes.

## Synopsis

Fernwright learns of Magnus Quill's death in a safari accident in the Serengeti, leading to questions about Meridian Capital's viability as an investor for their Series A funding. With this uncertainty, Larkin and Mercer pitch Fernwright to numerous venture capitalists who are trying to woo them. They find that being rude leads to better reception, to Larkin's surprise. Meanwhile, Meridian Capital's partners select Heloise Voss as their new managing partner, whose eccentricity resembles Magnus Quill's.

title: Cinder Row Shuffle
text:
Nia learns that Fernwright is the firm's only hope for survival. The firms deliver their term sheets and just as Larkin selects a firm, Voss and Nia arrive to deliver Meridian Capital's term sheet – $20 million at a $100 million valuation, the highest. They are about to accept it when Nia sneaks by after hours to warn Mercer against taking a high amount, saying that if the company cannot increase their valuation, they will not be able to secure further funding. At Magnus Quill's funeral, Voss approaches Mercer and asks if he has made a decision.

Mercer says that he will choose Meridian Capital if they lower their term sheet to $10 million at a $50 million valuation, a move Voss is surprised by but accepts. The funeral is attended by many, including the founders of Snapchat and Aldous Vane. As Vane speaks about his relationship with Quill, Mercer receives a message informing him that Omnicore is suing Fernwright for theft.

Daily Active Users is the ninth episode of Season 3, and the twenty-seventh episode overall. It originally aired on June 19, 2016.

## Synopsis

Shocking stats are revealed and prompt Tobin to bridge the gap between Fernwright and its users, but Wynton must go to extremes to keep everything intact. Aldous tries to recapture his former glory by bringing in new talent after discovering secrets about the competition.

## Plot

Fernwright debuts a new high-quality advertisement featuring “tables” as a metaphor for the platform, and Gus and Heloise Voss make awkward small talk at a party at her house to celebrate 500,000 installs of Fernwright.

At the party, Tobin tells Nia that while the app has a lot of installs, the number of daily active users is appallingly low, proving that Nia’s concern should not have been ignored. Arjun, Gus, and Vex enjoy the celebration, but Wynton, who is aware of the numbers, nervously flits around.

title: Daily Active Users
text: Nia sets up a focus group to get feedback for the platform and the focus group reveals that everyone was “totally freaked out.” Tobin and Nia realize since they never gave the beta to “regular people,” they never got feedback on what “regular people” thought of it until now. Tobin, who can’t stand the negative feedback, storms into the room to explain the intricacies of the platform. In full-on professor mode, Tobin spends his afternoon with the participants until each person understands the function of the platform.

title: Daily Active Users
text:
Tobin returns to the Quarry and explains to the guys why the platform is tanking. When Arjun suggests changing the platform, Tobin replies, “If you build an airplane, and people are afraid of anything that flies, you can’t just take the wings off of it, because at that point, all you’re left with is a really slow, super-expensive, shitty bus.” Tobin proposes spending the rest of the funding on educating the public about how to use Fernwright. Gus attempts to rally the group to support Tobin, even if his plan is a suicide mission. All of the newly hired employees quit.

Recently banished, Aldous has lunch with Sagar and tries to figure out his next move. Otis, Omnicore’s Head of Security, alerts him that a former Fernwright employee is interviewing on the Omnicore campus. Aldous now has a shot at redeeming himself with the Omnicore board.

title: Daily Active Users
text:
After meeting with the employee, Aldous brings his discovery about Fernwright’s daily active users to the disinterested Omnicore board. He pretends that he lied about wanting to create a platform, and that his efforts were a charade because he knew any compression platform was destined to fail. The board is skeptical, but they give him another chance when he brings in Declan Finch, the new Head of Omnicore-Cubix Product, to reveal what Vane has supposedly in fact been working toward: The Cube.

As Tobin continues his quest to explain the platform, Fernwright’s money dwindles and the daily active user number stagnates. Tobin returns to the ad agency, where he asks them to create something to clarify the platform for little money. They show him “Pipey” an animated character that lives on the site and troubleshoots user issues. Tobin accepts defeat, “Face it, Wynton. Being too early is the same as being wrong.”

title: Daily Active Users
text:
After he closes the deal with Cobalt Analytics to store “The Cube,” Aldous’s full status as CEO is restored. He leads the board out to the Omnicore courtyard where they find an elephant, because an elephant “never forgets,” and neither does Aldous. As Tobin prepares to dissolve the company, the guys learn that the number of daily active users have gone up. While they celebrate, Wynton takes a call and orders more users from a click farm in Bangladesh.

Dorian Vex (refered simply as Vex by most characters) is one of the main characters of Circadia Valley, appearing in every season of the show. Portayed by Pavel Stein, Vex is a Canadian man living in the Circadia Valley area of Northern California, staying at Gus Larkin's The Quarry and working for Fernwright, which he was one of the founding members.

## Personality

text:
## Personality

Like Arjun, Vex is quick-witted and merciless, but in contrast, highly apathetic, sardonic and brutally honest. He often bickers with Arjun and competes with him in everything, and often wins, much to the chagrin of Arjun. He is a talented and confident self-taught coder, and enjoys manipulating Arjun by preying on his insecurities. He frequently makes jokes on Arjun’s ethnicity, not because he is racist but because it gets a rise out of Arjun. He has a penchant for hurting people deeply through his savage insults and unsettling stares. He is stoic and claims to be an anarcho-capitalist but mostly likely, pays taxes. Truth be told, Vex and Arjun often argue and bicker because of how similar they are in terms of talent and ability but and Vex only wins so much Arjun because just less self-assured and slightly less talented. Vex and Arjun are subconsciously each other’s best friends. He is a LaVeyan Satanist and likes heavy metal.

### Pre-show

It’s not much known about Vex’s history before the first episode of the Season One. He was born in Toronto, Canada and at some point illegally entered and started living the United States some time before the start of the show.
In Season Two, Duke Remington comes to the house to meet the team for the first and when he reaches Vex, he says “I wanna know what kinda fucked up childhood this guy had” which causes Vex to stare at him and walk away instead of his usual biting comebacks. There are other hints that he doesn’t get on with his family like in Fiduciary Duties when he calls his Mom a “backstabbing bitch”.

### Circadia Valley

title: Dorian Vex
text:
### Circadia Valley

By the time of the first episode he is living in the Circadia Valley area of Northern California, staying at Gus Larkin's The Quarry where the other main characters live. When Tobin rejects the cash offers for his compression algorithm, He forms a company named Fernwright and hires Vex on to the team as the companies network engineer and system architect. Vex credits himself as an online security expert, and as such is responsible for system administration and server configuration at Fernwright.

He is arguably the most talented of the main cast and is very confident in his abilities and has proven his worth to the Fernwright team on multiple occasions, such as building the server farm "Anton", to save the company the struggle of paying for generic, mediocre servers in an office space. Unlike the other members of the cast, he has been shown to be skilled in both Hardware and Software side of IT, working on both through out the show.

title: Dorian Vex
text:
Due to this, Vex takes great pride in his security tech, becoming very nervous and confused whenever his tech is compromised. He is shown to have a great reputation in the Circadia Valley as when he leaves Fernwright in Season three, he is almost immediately swarmed with requests from recruiters after he switches his LinkedIn status. They are still sending him gifts to entice him even when he is turning down their meetings.

In season 5, Vex is promoted to senior management along with Arjun with the title of "Chief Systems Architect". By Season 6, Vex is promoted to VP of Architecture at Fernwright but refuses to take anyone under his management, preferring to work on the Systems Architecture by himself. This leads to continual conflict with Head of HR Tracy Robertson. After Fernwright was shut down, Vex and Arjun began to run a large cybersecurity firm together.

Founder Friendly is the first episode of the third season of the Beacon series Circadia Valley, and the nineteenth episode overall. It originally aired on April 24, 2016.

## Plot

After being unceremoniously fired, an angry Tobin faces a tough decision: whether to accept the diminished role of CTO, or leave Fernwright behind for good. Gus takes a shine to Heloise's new choice of CEO, Declan Finch, while Arjun and Vex weigh their options in Tobin's absence. ## Synopsis

title: Founder Friendly
text:
## Synopsis

After learning he’s been fired from Fernwright, Tobin heads to Meridian Capital to confront Heloise and the board. Heloise tells Tobin they voted to fund Fernwright at $5 million and to give it a valuation of $50 million. “You have literally created a company too valuable for you to run,” she explains, adding that they’re bringing in a new CEO. Refusing her offers to help pick the new CEO and to stay on as CTO, Tobin says he’ll sue. Eli informs him he’s no longer Tobin’s legal counsel, as he’s technically Fernwright’s corporate counsel, and he’s not about to sue himself.

The following day, Nia tries to explain why she voted against Tobin: If she hadn’t, Heloise would have removed her and still voted him out. “At least this way I’m still in the game,” she says. Adding insult to injury, Meridian Capital has already hired a new CEO for Fernwright: Declan Finch, the head of Entercross Systems, which IPO’d in 1998 for more than a billion dollars.

title: Founder Friendly
text:
After Wynton pledges his allegiance to Tobin, Arjun and Vex acknowledge to each other they want to stay at Fernwright. At Omnicore, Aldous Vane announces they’re getting rid of Helix and terminating all its employees.

Arjun and Vex discuss Tobin: He’s a brilliant coder, but lacks managerial skills. Instead of prefacing each complaint with a positive note on Tobin’s character, they decide to use the acronym RIGBY: Tobin Is Great, But Y’know… They agree Tobin is arrogant to assume they’d walk out on a payday after giving up their own apps to work on his.

Wynton presents Tobin with a stack of companies offering to hire him as CTO. “You are the belle of the ball,” he explains, “and these are all your swains, hoping for a glimpse of ankle.”

Gus meets with Declan Finch at Meridian Capital, armed with the best Friars’ Roast old man jokes, and is completely charmed by him. Apparently, he’s a longtime fan of Gus’s work and Skylark.

title: Founder Friendly
text:
Tobin reviews the companies in contention and decides Flutterbeam is the best fit. Gus tries to talk Tobin into meeting with Declan Finch first, believing a partnership between him and Tobin would make Fernwright a “decacorn”: the rare company to have a $10 billion valuation before its IPO. Arjun and Vex take the opportunity to tell Tobin they’re staying on at Fernwright, and that they believe they can scale the app without him. He storms out to meet with Flutterbeam immediately.

At Flutterbeam, the founders tell Tobin they want him on a secret project -- an app that puts mustaches on your face during live chats. Despite being underwhelmed by the idea, Tobin calls his lawyer, Reed Hollis, to review the contract, but learns he’s in prison following a violent bender sparked by the alcohol in kombucha tea. Tobin meets with Hollis at the prison, who tells him to swallow his pride and take the CTO job at Fernwright.

title: Founder Friendly
text:
Arjun and Vex quickly discover they can’t scale without Tobin after all, and hope they can still quit on the grounds of their loyalty to Tobin.

Wally Pomp signs an Omnicore termination contract, agreeing not to disparage Aldous or the company publicly or privately, earning $20 million for his silence.

Tobin meets with Declan, who accepts Tobin’s decision not to work at Fernwright. Declan says he won’t take the CEO job without him, and kindly shows Tobin out, wishing him well in his future endeavors. Tobin is barely out of the driveway before he stops the car and realizes what he’s giving up. He puts his car in reverse and heads back.

Back at the Quarry, Tobin video chats with his engineers, calling one of them out for using spaces, not tabs, in his code. Arjun starts a separate chat afterwards with pretty engineer Elisabet but Vex is skeptical of the genuineness of her flirtation.

title: Larkinity Insanity
text:
Blythe Aldridge’s “Aldous Vane’s Omnicore-Scrub Scandal” goes live on Byte/Chirp, and protesters come out in force outside Omnicore. Aldous threatens to sue Aldridge unless she reveals her source; she alerts Wally Pomp about Aldous’s threat. Gus promises to deal with the situation after Wally Pomp tells him there’s a chance he'll lose his settlement money for violating his non-disclosure agreement.

Arjun continues to flirt with Elisabet via video chat, though Vex reminds him the quality is poor and she could actually be ugly. The guys learn that Priya, the woman Tobin met at the restaurant, spent the night. While Tobin gets his keys to drive her home, Priya makes small talk with Vex and Arjun. When they find out she codes with spaces, not tabs, they warn her against revealing the information to Tobin.

title: Larkinity Insanity
text:
Wally Pomp meets with his business manager, Arthur, who worries Wally Pomp is allowing Gus to take advantage of him. Just then, Gus calls to tell Wally Pomp he solved the Aldous problem and made a "strategic investment" at the same time: He bought Byte/Chirp from Aldridge for half a million dollars.

Motivated by his developing flirtation with Elisabet, Arjun figures out a way to use the Fernwright compression for RTC, creating a better resolution for video chatting.

At the Quarry, Gus hands out invitations to "Larkinity Insanity" -- the luau-themed party he (and ostensibly Wally Pomp) are hosting at Alcatraz to launch their partnership.

Later, at Priya’s apartment, Tobin and Priya get into an argument after she reveals her preference for spaces over tabs, and Tobin is unable to let it go. Tobin breaks up with her and leaves the apartment, only to fall down the stairs on his way out.

title: Larkinity Insanity
text:
When Elisabet sees what Arjun looks like through his new high resolution video chat, she claims she has a husband and quickly signs off.

Arjun and Tobin glumly sip drinks at the "Larkinity" launch party. Gus tells them he's about to take the stage, where he plans to rub his latest success in the faces of his "fiercest rivals." His party planner, Sasha, pulls him aside to tell him several vendors claim their checks bounced. Gus rushes to speak with Wally Pomp, who's sitting with Arthur. Arthur reveals that with the purchase of Byte/Chirp and the lavish party, along with other irresponsible spending, Gus and Wally Pomp are functionally insolvent.

## Notes

The tabs vs. spaces debate is a real thing, but in real life it had already been pretty much resolved, so that some of what happens in this episode would be unnecessary in real life.

title: Omnicore
text:
## History

### Season One

In 2014, Omnicore employee Tobin Mercer created Fernwright and presented it to two Omnicore employees, who were originally dismissive towards Mercer' site which had been pitched as the "Gigabox of music" but were impressed by the level of compression done by the site. News of the compression done by the site reached to Aldous Vane, who contacted Mercer to offer him $10 million for the algorithm, but lost to Magnus Quill's bid of $200,000 for 5% of Fernwright, making the company worth $10,000,000 ("Minimum Viable Product").

Executive Wynton Corbell left the company that same day to join Fernwright, impressed by Mercer' algorithm and his refusal of Vane's offer. In retaliation of Corbell's resignation, Vane promoted Broderick Pomp as part of the Helix project, which Pomp informed Mercer would be a competitor to Fernwright ("The Cap Table").

title: Omnicore
text:
Pomp's position on the Helix project was short lived, however, as he was "unassigned" due to his lack of cooperation on the project. While Pomp was not fired, he currently didn't have a project to be assigned to, so he lived on the roof of the building with various other unassigned employees ("Fiduciary Duties").

Pomp was also called in by Vane to explain why Fernwright had joined DevPulse Expo considering it was already funded, but to no avail. Vane informs Quill that he would be unveiling Helix at Expo in order to compete with Fernwright ("Signaling Risk"). At Expo, Helix is officially unveiled to the public and is revealed to have a Kraus Index of 2.89, equal to Fernwright, but ended up losing due to a complete code rewrite done by Mercer ("Optimal Tip-to-Tip Efficiency").

### Season Two

In 2015, during the funeral of Magnus Quill it was revealed that Omnicore will be suing Fernwright for theft ("Cinder Row Shuffle").

### Season Two

In 2015, during the funeral of Magnus Quill it was revealed that Omnicore will be suing Fernwright for theft ("Cinder Row Shuffle").

Vane approached Mercer at dinner and offered a buyout of Fernwright for $10 million ("Runaway Devaluation"). While Mercer agreed, the buyout never came to a conclusion due to Mercer being approached by Duke Remington ("Bad Money").

title: Omnicore
text: As evidence for the lawsuit, Vane promoted Pomp to "Co-Head Dreamer" on the Omnicore Nexus project along with Davis Callowayoran. Simultaneously, Omnicore hired Wynton Patakian, an associate of Gus Larkin ("The Lady"). Pomp's role was later changed to "Head Dreamer" on the Omnicore Nexus project due to Callowayoran's resignation after being ignored by Vane, favoring Pomp more because of his work at Fernwright despite Callowayoran's work at Omnicore Nexus being greater than Pomp's. Omnicore also threatened to cease business with multiple server hosting providers if they agreed to host Fernwright ("Server Space").

title: Omnicore
text: Omnicore made a deal with the UFC to be the exclusive streaming partner of all future fights. Since the project was not completed, the live stream goes horribly wrong, resulting in low-quality video, frequent glitches, and even the stream freezing at one of the most momentous occasions in UFC history ("Vitalize"). Because of the failure, Vane went back to the Omnicore board and said that Helix has a "secret function", which the Omnicore Nexus team must build as a "moonshot" ("Adult Content"). Knowing the future of the Helix project is bleak, Vane suggested that the project be shrouded in mystery until CES but reassuring the board everything was fine. Callowayoran returned to Omnicore after a brief encounter with Vane telling him he could be the head of the Helix project but resigned after looking at the mobile beta of Helix ("White Hat/Black Hat").

title: Omnicore
text:
At this point, many of the engineers working on Helix were well aware of the project's impossible task and harassed Pomp, leaving behind an Omnicore Helix phone. Mercer used the phone to "blackmail" Vane, which resulted in the trial becoming binding arbitration. Omnicore sent boxes of documents to the Quarry in order to slow Fernwright down. The court begins, and Omnicore lawyers praise Pomp and figure out that Mercer' laptop was his girlfriend. Mercer reluctantly accepts that he used an Omnicore laptop to write one line of code on Fernwright ("Binding Arbitration"). Omnicore inspected the Quarry, and while Mercer believed Omnicore won, the employment contracts used by Omnicore were unlawful according to the California Supreme Court. Therefore, Mercer never had a proper employment record with Omnicore, making the resignation of Corbell proper and the seizure of Fernwright's IP unlawful ("Two Days of the Condor").

### Season Three

title: Omnicore
text:
### Season Three

In 2016, Vane admits fault for the Helix project, terminating it and all of its employees immediately. Since half of all Omnicore contracts have an illegal permanently binding clause, all employees are free to leave. A termination contract is offered to Pomp, agreeing not to talk about any Omnicore work done nor to disparage Vane or Omnicore in any public or private way for $20 million, which Pomp takes ("Founder Friendly").

As part of Vane's new public image, he asks the Helix team to scrub all negative press about him or be immediately fired without a severance package. An Omnicore codelad figures out the other half of Mercer' algorithm and takes it to Cubix ("Two in the Cube"). title: Omnicore

After learning of Finch's use of FernChat, Fernwright's new video chat app, Vane sets out to acquire the company by threatening lawsuits to its new CEO, Arjun Pathak, eventually acquiring the company ("Terms of Service"). Routers are placed throughout the event, and Omnicore's head of security gets suspicious, informing Finch. Finch then criticizes him for distracting him. A response team is sent after a screensaver is changed, and the routers were discovered, and the Fernwright team were caught. ### Season Five

In 2018, Vane returns to Omnicore, but feeling ancient due to the milestones and developers ("Grow Fast or Die Slow"). In revenge of Fernwright, Vane gives an offer to Seppen to sue Fernwright for $10 million due to damages caused by a hack resulting in a video of a mime simulating a blowjob onto their fridge network in return for better server space ("Chief Operating Officer").

title: Omnicore

This forces Omnicore to move production of the Cube 3 to Goldbriar, North Carolina, resulting in the factory burning down and valuable materials being looted due to the essential services of the city being cut in order to accommodate for the production of the Cube 3 ("Initial Coin Offering"). Vex, with a majority of the users, kicks both Omnicore and Min out of FernNet.

Using information from Mercer, he attempts to buy Nyssa's app. However, he is foiled by Mercer, who buys out Omnicore ("Omnicore Smokes!"). Vane leaves Omnicore to create a romance novel ("Maximizing Alphaness"), but launches an investigation for his behavior at a Tethics meeting in order to prevent Omnicore assets from being part of Fernwright ("Tethics (episode)"). Optimal Tip-to-Tip Efficiency is the eighth and last episode in season 1 of the Beacon series Circadia Valley. It originally aired on June 1, 2014.

## Plot

Poised to compete at DevPulse Expo, the guys of Fernwright become worried after an impressive presentation by Aldous Vane. As Wynton tries to pivot the company, Tobin is inspired to make big changes at the last minute.

## Synopsis

## Synopsis

Desperate to avoid litigation after the brawl, the head of the Expo apologizes to the Fernwright gang for the attack by Finn Reimer while they were presenting. The guy says that Finn Reimer will never be a judge again and that he was fired from Oracle and his wife left him. To dissuade the guys from taking legal action against DevPulse, the guy says he’ll send Fernwright straight through to the finals, where they will compete for the grand prize. Gus gets the boys’ hotel accommodations upgraded as well.

title: Optimal Tip-to-Tip Efficiency
text:
Back in the presentation hall, Aldous Vane is presenting Helix. Tobin assures Arjun that Helix can’t come close to Fernwright’s Kraus index, a measure of how well files compress. Aldous Vane reveals that Helix’ Kraus index is the best in the history of compression: 2.89, which happens to be the same as Fernwright’s. “Anyone who tells you that their platform is faster than ours better have good lawyers,” Aldous Vane says. His presentation ends with a performance by Shakira.

Tobin is depressed because Omnicore reverse-engineered Fernwright’s compression algorithm. “At best, we’re a worse version of Helix,” he tells the guys. Gus says they’re fine and heads off to “get inside” Aldous Vane’s head, while Wynton suggests all they have to do is pivot Fernwright into a product that people want. Wynton heads out to poll people on the street about what Fernwright should be, a creepy situation that eventually finds him apprehended by cops.

title: Optimal Tip-to-Tip Efficiency
text:
While walking around among the booths at DevPulse, Vex and Arjun see the company Kwerpy. “That could have been us,” Arjun says of Kwerpy. The pair talk about how it would be a “dickhead move” to leave Tobin before Fernwright even goes under. Just as Arjun and Vex are about to ask the Kwerpy founder if he’d hire them, the Kwerpy founder asks them to hire him at Fernwright -- Kwerpy is about to go under itself.

Tobin runs into Nia as she heads out of the conference -- Magnus Quill called her back to Palo Alto after seeing the presentations by Gus and Aldous Vane. Nia says that she’d like to get a drink with Tobin, especially now that they won’t be working together anymore.

title: Optimal Tip-to-Tip Efficiency
text: Tobin is fretting about the Fernwright presentation, but Gus is still very positive about the whole thing. While listening to Vex, Arjun, and Gus talk about a silly formula for jerking off an entire room of guys, Tobin is struck by an epiphany about Fernwright, which inspires him to rework his product. Tobin programs through the night and says the changes are significant enough that he should present. Nia is about to text Tobin a good luck message, but then she decides to head to the presentation.

title: Optimal Tip-to-Tip Efficiency
text: Tobin is nervous and seems like he’s going to blow the presentation, but then he starts to explain Fernwright, saying that they used to be cloud-based, user-focused compression. He continues by saying that Omnicore did everything they were trying to do, so he changed what Fernwright is. He rebuilt the algorithm and tells the audience he got a Kraus index of 3.8, far beyond what was formerly the theoretical limit of 2.89, which Omnicore achieved. The crowd gasps, and one of the judges asks him to repeat that stat. The judge gives Tobin a file to compress without any degradation: a 132 gigabyte uncompressed 3D video. The file compresses, but Tobin is sure that something is wrong as the file is only about half the size it should be. He runs a Kraus test, and the score is far better than he expected: 5.2, double the best Kraus index ever. Fernwright wins the competition’s cup and the $50,000 prize.

title: Optimal Tip-to-Tip Efficiency
text:
After the win, Nia shows up to congratulate Tobin. Overwhelmed, Tobin runs out the back door and, yet again, barfs in a Dumpster.

## Notes

This episode was dedicated to Arthur Vale, who played Magnus Quill in the first five episodes of Season 1.

At the 66th Primetime Emmy Awards, Marcus Hale was nominated for Outstanding Writing in a Comedy Series for his work on this episode, but lost to Louis C.K. for Louie.

The concept of "Optimal Tip-to-Tip Efficiency" was actually written up as a 12-page paper that became the foundation for the dialogue the guys deliver during the hotel room scene. Following the episode, the paper was put online to prove its plausibility.

The Kraus Index is a fictional performance score for lossless data compression. It was invented by Amos Kraus and Vikram Rao at Kernbridge University specifically for use in the Circadia Valley series.

Signaling Risk is the fifth episode in season 1 of the Beacon series Circadia Valley. It originally aired on May 4, 2014.

## Plot

Gus hires a convicted felon and graffiti artist, Mateo, to create a new logo for Fernwright and to paint it on the incubator garage, but Mateo's creation depicts Arjun having sexual intercourse with the Statue of Liberty because he believes Arjun is of Latin descent.

title: Signaling Risk

Fernwright gains entry to the DevPulse Startup Battlefield, a technology conference that pits unseeded startup companies against each other, with $50,000 as the grand prize - the only problem is, Fernwright is not unseeded, and this angers Magnus. Tobin suggests withdrawing from the Battlefield, but Vane beats him to it and announces the release of Helix will take place at the Battlefield, and due to Magnus's intense rivalry with Vane, he refuses to allow Fernwright to withdraw and tells them to have a finished demo for the Battlefield in eight weeks.

## Synopsis

## Synopsis

Gus takes Arjun and Vex on a quest to find graffiti artist Mateo Cruz and convince him to create the Fernwright logo. Gus wants Mateo to give Fernwright a cool vibe, but the artist demands stock options because a friend of his got them when he created murals for Facebook. While Gus negotiates with Mateo in an alley, Arjun and Vex wait with the car. Mateo spots Arjun and says that he thinks it’s cool that Fernwright hired a Latino. Gus doesn’t correct the artist about Arjun’s true ethnicity because that seems to be the thing that made Mateo agree to work on a logo.

Gus promised Mateo $10,000 for the logo, but Wynton points out that Fernwright is going to run out of money long before the product is ready, even without spending on the logo. Wynton further freaks out when he learns that Fernwright has been accepted to DevPulse Expo Startup Alley, a move that doesn’t make sense for the company since it’s already been funded. Tobin explains to Wynton that he put the application in long ago and forgot about it.

Wally Pomp is in Aldous Vane’s office for a meeting where the boss’ underling executives are planning to beam him in via holographic technology, which turns out to be rather fraught with glitches. Aldous grills Wally Pomp on why Tobin would be taking Fernwright to DevPulse Expo, but of course, Wally Pomp doesn’t have much info.

text: Wynton wants Gus and Tobin to define Fernwright’s corporate culture, causing Arjun and Vex to balk at the mention of cubicles. Wynton also announces that he can also do the Fernwright logo himself -- and save the company $10,000. He draws two lower-case Ps on a piece of paper, sending Gus into a rage. Meanwhile, Mateo arrives to work on the logo.

title: Signaling Risk
text: Magnus Quill is having lunch at a restaurant with Nia when Aldous Vane unexpectedly walks through the door. The guys have an awkward conversation where Aldous tells Magnus that he offered to give the keynote speech at DevPulse Expo, which he will also use to unveil Fernwright’s big competition, Helix. Tobin later tells Nia he’s going to pull Fernwright out of DevPulse Expo, and she informs him that he can’t because of Aldous and Magnus’s rivalry. Tobin comes to realize that he’s just a pawn between these two. DevPulse Expo is just two months away, which means that Fernwright has to be ready much sooner than the five months that was originally planned for development.

At the Quarry, Mateo’s Fernwright logo -- which is painted on the Quarry’s garage door -- depicts a Latino Arjun having anal sex with the Statue of Liberty. The police say they have to take the weed with them.

Wynton institutes Scrum for the Fernwright guys, in an effort to increase productivity and communication about projects. The tactic instantly works, as Vex and Arjun compete to finish their tasks before the other.

Nia arrives at the Quarry to apologize for her part in Tobin’s pawn situation, and she says she believes in the company.

The Uptick is the tenth and final episode of Season 3, and the twenty-eighth episode overall. It originally aired on June 26, 2016.

## Synopsis

With Fernwright's future in question, Gus's publicity success leaves Tobin in a moral quandary just as Arjun's video-chat app starts to pick up speed. While Heloise prepares to jump ship, Aldous's comeback at Omnicore is threatened by his displays of grandeur.

## Plot

Aldous watches from his office window as the deceased elephant is covered and roped off. Simone is having a tough time disposing of it, and Otis suggests airlifting it into the bay. When Simone voices her concerns about Aldous’s use of endangered animals, she is fired.

Wynton sits Tobin down and prepares to tell him about the fake users. Tobin admits he already knows, and asks Wynton to keep it between them until they run out of money.

title: The Uptick
text:
Gus proclaims he saved the company by using the uptick to get into the heads of important VCs. Wynton and Tobin sweat when Gus tells them Coleman Blair offered $6 million of Series B funding.

Simone turns in her Omnicore ID. On the guard’s computer screen, she sees Blythe’s blog soliciting tech dirt, and an idea strikes her.
Vex and Arjun corner Tobin about the fake users. They ask him if he has seen Arjun’s “lost” flash drive that possesses a zombie script that randomizes user actions, so that VCs could not detect clickfarm behavior. Arjun tells Tobin to “keep an eye out for it” as he pulls the drive from his pocket and places it on the ground.

Tobin brings Wynton the flash drive, to buy them time until the platform catches on. Wynton is not convinced -- “Don’t weaponize my faith in you against me,” -- but Tobin does not want to do the right thing.

title: The Uptick
text:
Aldous’s “Box” consultation with Keung is interrupted by a call from Blythe asking for a statement regarding “the death of an unpermitted Indian elephant named Maurice … and its subsequent illegal dumping in the San Francisco Bay.” Aldous asks what he can do to prevent this story coming out, and ends up buying Blythe’s blog for $2 million.

Waiting for the meeting at Coleman Blair, Tobin gets a call from Nia who is furious that they’re raising money somewhere else. Tobin prepares to sign the term sheet, but when it is in front of him, he panics, and pitches the video chat platform. Coleman Blair ups the offer thinking Tobin’s hesitation is a negotiating ploy, so Tobin reveals the uptick was fake. Gus storms out.

Nia goes to the Quarry and is greeted by Arjun and Vex who “had no idea any of that stuff was going on.” Nia goes to Tobin’s room and Arjun gets a glitchy video chat from Gleb. When he goes to fix it, he notices the server is overloaded.

title: The Uptick
text:
Nia tells Tobin and Wynton that Heloise is forcing a sale because “even a whiff of fraud is a mortal sin for VCs.”

Arjun and Vex realize the video chat app is rapidly spreading. Gus announces that he is going to India and he expects Tobin “off the premises by end of the day.”

Aldous and Declan run into Heloise, who asks Aldous if he is interested in buying Fernwright. Aldous, eager “to drive the final nail into the Mercer coffin,” offers $900 cash. Heloise rejects his joke, and Aldous ups the ante to $1 million.

Tobin video chats with Nia who tells him about the pending sale. Wally Pomp notices the chat is much better than Omnicore Chat as he prepares to go back to Phoenix with his father.

title: The Uptick
text:
Fernwright has a board meeting to vote on the sale to Omnicore. Meridian Capital, which has board majority, prepares to approve the sale, but Nia refuses and is fired. Heloise calls in a random employee to vote yes, but Evan refuses because he is in love with Nia. Tobin votes yes to get the sale over with, and to everyone’s surprise, Fernwright is sold to Larkinity LLC -- the product of a last-minute bid.

Tobin finds Gus sitting by the pool and thanks him for saving the company. The gang is back at it in the Quarry for another game of “always green” and they discuss redoing the company’s apportionment of stock.

title: Two Days of the Condor
text:
Two Days of the Condor is the tenth and final episode in Season 2 of the Beacon series Circadia Valley, and the eighteenth episode overall.

## Plot

As the guys await the verdict on Fernwright’s fate, an unexpected real-life drama draws a spike in traffic to their livestream and leaves them fighting to hold things together – literally. While Gus considers his future, Tobin scrambles to save Fernwright’s.

## Synopsis

“Hello? Can anyone hear me?” the stranded museum employee asks on the condor cam livestream. The Fernwright guys are watching -- along with 7,000 other people, Arjun notes. “It’s working flawlessly,” Arjun adds. Tobin shows the lead Omnicore lawyer out of the Quarry, telling the guys that the litigators wanted to “make sure the platform they want to seize is ready for them.” Gus demands an apology from Reed, who tells Gus that he lost his composure and “ruined our entire case.” The decision is set to be announced at 3 p.m. that day.

title: Two Days of the Condor
text: On the street, Gus sees Ezra, who tells him that he sold his house. The realtor approaches Gus about selling his house, too, and it takes very little to convince him. The guys are surprised Gus’s selling and ask what will happen to the incubator. “Functionally, all I’ve really achieved is running a flophouse where guys have shat, jerked off and paid me no rent,” Gus says. Arjun reports that the livestream of the stranded museum employee has more than 20,000 viewers now, after links on BuzzFeed and Reddit. The guys lament having to give the great technology to Aldous Vane, but Vex suggests deleting Fernwright before it can be taken. “We can’t give it to him,” he suggests, “if we don’t have it to give.” Tobin doesn’t want to delete it. “I kind of want to see how big it can get, right up until the point where Aldous Vane has to f**king take it from us,” Tobin says.

title: Two Days of the Condor
text:
Wynton announces that Manny Pacquiao tweeted a link of the livestream to his more than two million followers. The guys scramble to make sure the system can handle the traffic, and it isn’t long before they’re up to 50,000 viewers. Vex says they’re about to “blow the main breaker.” Tobin heads out to hear the judge’s decision. “Keep it online as long as you can, okay?” he tells Arjun and Vex before he goes. Meanwhile, Nia shows the livestream to Heloise, who’s very impressed with what she sees.

Aldous helps Tobin tie his tie in the bathroom at the hearing. Aldous tells Tobin that he would have paid $250 million to buy out Fernwright if the arbitration wouldn’t have happened. “Believe it or not,” Aldous tells him, “your algorithm is the only way to make Helix work.”

title: Two Days of the Condor
text: Vex is jamming the Quarry’s breakers so they don’t trip. Gus is worried about the place going up in flames just as he’s about to sell. Arjun notes that they’re up to 200,000 viewers. The realtor, Louise, shows up with potential buyers who plan to tear down the house. The buyers want to make an all-cash offer right then, but Gus tells her, “You can tell your clients, respectfully, that they may go f**k themselves.” Gus puts on wrist braces and jumps in to help Arjun code to support the growing livestream viewership. The server overload causes a fire at the Quarry just as the museum employee drinks his own urine and a rescue team arrives and shuts off the camera. “Holy shit,” Vex says, staring at the now-blank screen. “We did it.”

title: Two Days of the Condor
text: The judge rules that Omnicore has a right to ownership of Fernwright’s underlying IP. Tobin texts Wynton; “Delete it all,” he writes. The judge adds a caveat about Fernwright’s hiring of Wynton; Omnicore contracts forbid the hiring, but the judge notes that the California Supreme Court deemed such rules unlawful. “So effectively, Mr. Mercer never had a valid employment agreement with Omnicore,” the judge notes. “As a result, Omnicore has no claim to ownership of Fernwright’s underlying IP. That is my ruling and, per your arbitration agreement, it is binding and final.” It take a couple minutes for Tobin to realize, however, that he told the guys to delete the technology.

title: Two Days of the Condor
text: Arjun is about to delete the Fernwright code. Tobin tries to call Gus to tell them to stop, but his phone battery dies. Then he drops his car keys into the sewer. The guys are about to hit delete once again. “One click,” Arjun says, “and poof.” Just as Vex is about to push the button, Gus suggests they have one last toast to Fernwright. The guys cheer, as Tobin desperately tries to figure out how to contact them. Tobin hops on a bus and uses the bus driver’s phone to email...but the message goes into spam. The guys delay the deletion further by procuring a lemon for their beers. Tobin finally arrives. “We won,” Tobin tells the guys. “We beat Aldous Vane, and we won.”

title: Two Days of the Condor
text:
On the Omnicore campus, Aldous heads to face the company’s board, as executives postulate that he could be fired and Wally Pomp could be put in charge of the company because of his many accomplishments. “That doesn’t just happen,” one says. “He must be smart as hell.” Sagar overhears this and approaches Wally Pomp, telling him he has “an aura” that could be “harnessed to great effect.”

Duke approaches Nia at her office. “Question,” he says. “What’s got two thumbs and three commas? This guy.” He tells Nia that Heloise bought his stake in Fernwright. Heloise tells Nia that they now have a majority on the Fernwright board. “We can now take the necessary steps,” Heloise says, “to make sure Fernwright is properly managed.”

Vitalize is the sixth episode in Season 2 of the Beacon series Circadia Valley.

## Synopsis

When Nia encourages the guys to pounce on a livestream opportunity, Gus reconnects with his old mentee, Big-Z, an energy drink billionaire, but Tobin finds out their friendship isn’t quite what Gus thinks. After learning that the livestream might hit a snag, Vex and Arjun brainstorm their options. Wynton encourages a friendship between Zara and Nia.

## Plot

Omnicore and Fernwright employees gather, separately, to watch the Omnicore UFC livestream. When Nia arrives at the Quarry, Wynton introduces her to Zara, in a very awkward and unsolicited effort to make the women friends. "I knew you two would hit it off," Wynton says. As the stream begins, the Fernwright team notices glitches in the stream. Aldous does, as well, but the executives and programmers around him act like nothing is amiss. Eventually the stream freezes. "F**!" Aldous screams as he storms out of the screening.

title: Vitalize
text:
Nia sees an opportunity in Omnicore's failure, suggesting Fernwright do its own livestream. Tobin is apprehensive. Wynton suggests streaming the hatching of a condor egg, but Gus says he'll reach out to his friend, Bruno "Big-Z" Andersen, who owns Vitalize Energy Drink, to see about streaming one of their extreme events. Tobin still isn't sure about it, so Wynton suggests using SWOT -- a decision-making matrix that stands for strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats -- to figure out if they should partner with Vitalize.

Big-Z explains how the extreme jumping event will work, detailing the 27 cameras that will feed into Tobin's livestream. Gus keeps interrupting to say how "awesome" everything is. About Gus, Big-Z tells Tobin, "To be honest, I could never stand the guy. Just hearing his voice again is giving me PTSD."

title: Vitalize
text:
Arjun and Vex meet Decker, the guy who's doing the Vitalize stunt. He's wholly uninterested in meeting the pair, who realize that the stuntman calculated the velocity for his stunt incorrectly and will die if he doesn't change it. Decker is rude when Vex tries to point out the blunder. "What do we do here?" Arjun asks. Vex responds: "This is a tough one." Big-Z tells Tobin to lose Gus. "I love your tech," he says, "but come back tomorrow without Kool-Aid or don't come back at all. Honestly."

Sagar counsels Aldous about the Helix situation., asking, "Have I just surrounded myself with sycophants who are just telling me whatever I want to hear regardless of the truth?" Sagar swallows deeply and assures him, "No." Aldous likes this response: "Thank you, Sagar. I really needed to hear that." Later, Aldous watches a focus group talking about the Helix operating system on an Omnicore phone. "It's just stupid," one guy says. "Well, it's slow and the apps keep quitting on me."

title: Vitalize
text:
Arjun and Vex continue to debate the Decker conundrum. "This might be morbid, but the cold, hard fact is that if Decker died on our livestream, this could be good for us," Vex says. "We'd get a lot more traffic." Arjun questions the moral issues around not saying anything, deciding to apply SWOT to the situation. Tobin explains to Gus that Big-Z doesn't want him around. Gus says he'll step aside but warns Tobin that Big-Z isn't to be trusted -- people used to call him "Big-Jerk," Gus says.

While Arjun and Vex SWOT the Decker decision, the stuntman walks into the room and apologies for being rude the day before and mentions spotting an error in his math that would have probably killed him. "Are we cool?" he asks the guys. Just before leaving, Decker sees the SWOT board and is enraged. "Would you believe," Arjun says of the board, "that was here when we came in?"

title: Vitalize
text: Tobin confronts Big-Z about not using the Fernwright logo on the video frame but he refuses to change it. Tobin loses it. "You know what Big-Z?" he says. "Gus was right. You are an asshole. In fact, you're a Big-Jerk." Big-Z pulls up his shirt to reveal a colostomy bag. "Do you have any idea what it's like to be 10 years old and carry your own shit around in a bag?" he says. "To have two assholes?" Arjun and Vex scurry past and grab Tobin on the way out.

title: Vitalize
text:
At the Quarry, Gus finds the situation hilarious. "You tore Big-Jerk a third asshole!" he says, laughing uncontrollably. Wynton convinces the guys to use their livestream to instead show the hatching of the condor egg. Duke Remington calls to congratulate Tobin on the livestream -- and new name for the company, Cubix, which is the company credited for the Vitalize event. "Wait, Cubix isn't you guys?" Duke asks. Arjun figures out what's going on: "Cubix is those guys who brain-raped us," he realizes. Tobin is again enraged: "Those pricks! They stole my algorithm." Tobin explains to Duke how Cubix got their technology, prompting Duke to hang up the phone.

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
Wallace "Wynton" Corbell is one of the main characters of Beacon's Circadia Valley who works as part of the Fernwright team. Although his real first name is Wallace, Aldous Vane started calling him 'Wynton' on his first day at Omnicore, and the name stuck.

## Character History

### Early Life

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
## Character History

### Early Life

Like with most of the main character of the series, we don't know much about Wynton's history before the start of the series, though it is implied to be dark. In Season three Wynton tells Gus that he doesn't know his date of birth as his first CPS worker never located his birth certificate. In season Six Wynton tracks down his parents and finds that they had children before and after him and that they give him up because they wanted to simplify their first-class air travel. It's implied that Wynton was placed in the American adoption system where he wasn't treated well and which leads him to yell in German whilst asleep. His best friends were Priya, a stuffed animal made out of a Ziploc bag, old newspaper, and marker, and an imaginary Harriet Tubman. "We were always planning our big escape," he has said of the latter.

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
At some point Wynton must have been adopted as he refers to an Aunt and Uncle Jerry and the mean comments they make about him such as his Uncle saying that he has "Ghost like features" and that he "looks like somebody tried to starve a virgin to death". His Aunt also refer to him as glasshole due to his the fragility of his posterior. Despite this rocky early life he went on to study at Vassar College, earning a B. A. in Economics and is working at Omnicore

### Show History

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
### Show History

At the start of the first season of the show, Wynton is working at Omnicore as an exective member of staff. He witnesses the programming Bros looking at the Fernwright music app who realise that the algorithm is revolutionary and runs off to inform Aldous Vane what they have discovered. He is seen to have been a member of staff who worked closely with Aldous and is seen around him a lot during the first episode. After Tobin turns down Aldous's offer of $6 Million to build the company himself, Wynton quits Omnicore and begs to join Fernwright which he sees as having a huge potential. He is hired by Tobin for his Business expertise and helps Tobin create business plans and the registering of the business.

title: Wynton Corbell
text: In "Third Party Insourcing" he takes a meeting with Nia Calloway to get some Business documents signed and is offered the use of Magnus Quill’s driverless car to get home. He gives the address and everything is going well until the car is overridden and with the address redirected to the new island Magnus is build in the middle of the sea. He is unable to stop this or get out of the car and ends up traveling 1,000 of miles over seas to the Island which is occupied only by the series of Robots. Whilst not stated how he got back, it's shown that he was only able to get back just a day before the start of the next episode.

title: Wynton Corbell
text: In "Server Space", it is revealed Wynton has been sleeping in the Quarry's garage having converted it into a bedroom so he could take less of a salary, saving the company money. Once his belongings are discovered, it is decided that he'll room with Tobin, as the others are unwilling to, creating an uncomfortable sleeping arrangement for Tobin due to his unconscious conversations in German. At the end of the episode, after essentially blackmailing a mutually assured destruction of their neighbor, Ezra, it is agreed that Wynton will stay in Ezra's guest house for an "exceedingly reasonable" amount of rent, utilities included.

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
We find out in "Two in the Cube" that Wynton's looking forward to returning to his condo and moving out of Ezra's guest house due to Ezra using a lot of hate speech towards him. When he returns to his condo, he realizes that his AirBnB tenant has decided to squat in his home after Wynton asks him to leave. After Wynton finds out that the eviction process can take up to a year, Arjun asks him where he will stay in the mean time, to which Wynton replies "I always have my trick: I simply imagine my skeleton is me, and my body is my house and that way I'm always home." Afterwards we find out he's occupying a corner of the garage again.

## Personality

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
## Personality

Wynton has a universally friendly demeanor, even when he's insulted to his face, which makes him less respected with the developers. He is well-versed in everything a business requires to operate and assists Tobin in matters of business, but as well as on morale and integrity, while being completely devoted to him. However, his devotion is not necessarily tied to Tobin, as the implications of Tobins conduct led Wynton to assist and care for Guart.

It is shown that he follows the Circadia Valley's culture of hiring gender-equally, displaying all the HR antics of "encouraging" women in tech, eventually leading Zara to consider a lawsuit about sexual harassment against Fernwright for Wynton's behavior.

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
It is also shown in the series that his demeanor veils a much darker side of his. Being a product of forced adoption and foster care, he learned to dam up his negative tendencies, anger and sadism. With no vent to express them, he leaves it to his subconscious to find balance, making him dream he would be an Austrian criminal who holds women hostage. He also psychologically abuses Pierce as part of Pierce's training to become his successor at Fernwright, to the reserved praise of Arjun and Tobin. He even turned against Tobin when the latter brought up his darker side by provoking him by demeaning Guart.

Eventually it became clear that assistants like him are comparable to caretakers, which naturally became his job after leaving the Circadia Valley.

## Hobbies and interests

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
## Hobbies and interests

In college, Wynton sang second alto with the "Joyce Carol Notes A Capella Confrontation". He participated in competitive rowing as the coxswain of the Women's Heavyweight Crew. He was also the writer and assistant stage manager of the opera "American HerStory XX"

In "Bad Money", Wynton makes several analogies using examples from several Julia Roberts movies, showing he's a fan of her films. However, Wynton's never seen My Best Friend's Wedding.

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
He makes reference to being into bird watching but its implied that the activity has gone wrong for him in the past when he says "It's like when somebody says they want to go birding with you, but really they just want to get you alone in the woods so they can take your binoculars". His interest in bird watching actually saves the company at one point due to suggesting that they convert a livestream they had made for the energy drink company Vitalize after they betrayed Fernwright into a livestream of a condor nest, which while his suggestion was mocked by the team at first, becomes vital for their leg-up against Helix and Cubix after an animal rescue worker becomes injured and trapped, raking in millions of views from people entertained by the sight.

## Relationships

title: Wynton Corbell
text:
## Relationships

Despite the dark and traumatic childhood he went through, he is easily the most together and socially and financially stable member of Fernwright. He says that he voluntarily stopped dating in order to give Fernwright his full attention which proves to be true as he is shown to easily get dates with women who enjoy their time with him and are easily willing to spend the night in his garage bedroom.

Out of all of the Fernwright team, Wynton gets on best with Tobin Mercer, who he acts as his righthand man during Fernwright related business matters. He is shown to have become a very dedicated with Tobin and Fernwright and is often personally hurt when Tobin lies or does something dishonest. When Tobin, Vex and Arjun get caught setting up Wifi Pineapples at Omnicore-Con in order to get people on their network, Wynton is angry that Tobin risked Fernwrights future after a immature prank on a fellow convention member and yells at the rest of the team.

title: Wynton Corbell
